subject.title: Stuck-session liveness monitor misclassifies healthy processing runs as stale during event-loop stalls

question: Should OpenClaw change the processing/no-activeWorkKind recovery policy now, or require a live/deterministic proof that healthy active runs can hit stale_session_state and abort_embedded_run during event-loop stalls first?
rationale: The source fallthrough is real, but existing tests intentionally recover this state and the issue explicitly labels the healthy-run abort mechanism as likely rather than confirmed.

options.title: Require proof first
options.body: Keep the issue open for a controlled gateway log or harness reproduction before changing stuck-session recovery semantics.

options.title: Patch classifier now
options.body: Approve a narrow classifier change for processing/no-activeWorkKind sessions and update tests to preserve only genuinely ownerless stale recovery.

options.title: Fold into broader liveness work
options.body: Track this edge under the active-run false-abort and event-loop-stall cluster rather than handling the classifier branch independently.

recommendation.title: Require proof first
recommendation.body: Keep the issue open for a controlled gateway log or harness reproduction before changing stuck-session recovery semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: obviyus has the most recent ownerless-lane recovery work on this exact runtime boundary.
